Council Minutes  02/10/2020
   On order of the Mayor, the regular meeting reconvened at 6:38

  Kennedy.

ROLL CALL:  Mayor Terry Tomek
 Councilmembers:  Vice Mayor Tyron Hampton
  Councilmember Victor Gordo

  Councilmember Gene Masuda
  Councilmember Margaret McAustin

  Staff:  City Manager Steve Mermell

CEREMONIAL MATTERS  They Mayor presented Patricia A. Coulter, President of the
  League of Women Voters - Pasadena Area Chapter, with a
  commendation on the Chapter's 1ooth Anniversary. Ms. Coulter
  expressed gratitude to the Mayor and City Council for recognizing
  their centennial celebration.

  Pablo Alvarado, representing National Day Laborer Organization
  Network (NDLON), distributed copies of a resolution and asked
  that the City Council adopt the resolution pledging to monitor 2020
  census data collection for breaches of confidentiality. Mayor
  Tomek responded that a discussion on the proposed resolution
  will be agendized at a future City Council meeting. The City
  Council spoke on the importance of responding to the 2020
  Census, thanked Mr. Alvarado for advocating for people of color,
  and spoke in support of agendizng the item for discussion. Mr.
  Wilson asked staff to return with information on a strategy to
  disseminate the resolution widely.

PUBLIC COMMENT ON  Debra Johnson, Pasadena resident, commented on various
MATTERS NOT ON THE  issues including: safe harbor parking, accommodations for
AGENDA  homeless individuals, and racial profiling.

  Alieka Monet Marcos Townsend, Pasadena resident, expressed
  concerns with abusive behavior and the lack of cleanliness at the
  Union Station Adult Center/Shelter.

  Councilmembers Kennedy and Madison requested that Code
  Compliance and Health staff follow up on the concerns expressed
  by the public speaker and schedule inspection visits. In response,
  City Manager Mermell stated that the appropriate staff will look
  into the issues that were raised.

Council Minutes  2  02/10/2020
   Okeyo Jumal, Pasadena resident, expressed concerns with the
  location of the Jackie Robinson plaque on Pepper Street, noting
  that it is difficult to find, requested that additional information be
  added to the plaque, and also that it be moved to a more
  prominent location. Councilmember Kennedy provided contact
  information for Rochelle Branch, Cultural Affairs Manager.

  Muna Busailah, representing the Pasadena Police Officers'
  Association, distributed literature and spoke on the lvis Moran
  judgement, Police Officers Bill of Rights violations, and the need
  to foster employee/employer relations.

  The following individuals expressed concerns and provided
  comments related to the termination of Fire Chief Bertral
  Washington:

  Allen Edson, President of the Pasadena National Association
  for the Advancement of Colored People
  Kim Miles, Pasadena resident

  Vice Mayor Hampton expressed concerns with the reassignment
  of Fire Chief Bertral Washington.

  Councilmember Kennedy also expressed concerns with the
  reassignment; spoke on the need to determine if Chief Bertral
  Washington's due process rights were violated; and requested
  information as to whether the City Manager consulted with any
  member of the City Council before taking on the reassignment.
  He stated the following for the record, "In terms of contravening or
  countermanding a decision by the City Manager, what rights does
  the Council have and would you be able to share those rights in
  public to reassign the Fire Chief back in his role that he was hired
  to do." and "For me, if you work in a City at that executive level, a
  department head level you should strongly consider living here.
  And the Fire Chief, unlike some other department heads ... and I've
  already hit this issue when I first came on the Council, made the
  decision to make a huge investment in this community, in
  purchasing a home and really be part of the fabric of life in
  Pasadena."

  In response to Councilmember Kennedy's Inquires related to
  Chief Bertral Washington's due rights, Michele Beal Bagneris, City
  Attorney/City Prosecutor, responded that the City Council can
  discuss certain prescribed items in closed session and will
  research if such a discussion is appropriate.

Council Minutes  3  02/10/2020
   Councilmember Gordo and the Mayor expressed concerns with
  any elected official inadvertently violating Chief Bertral
  Washington rights under general personnel policy and procedure
  laws, including the Fire Fighters Bill of Rights.

  In response to public and Councilmembers comments, City
  Manager Mermell responded, that all employees have a right to
  privacy as it relates to their employment, including Fire Chief
  Bertral Washington, and therefore stated he will not comment on
  a personnel matter.

  Beverly Shanahan, requested assistance with her eviction from
  the property at 230 E. California Boulevard.

Council Minutes  8  02/10/2020
   (2) Uphold the Board of Zoning Appeal's decision and approve
  Affordable Housing Concession Permit No. 11869.

  David Reyes, Director of Planning and Community Development,
  Talyn Mirzakhanian, Principle Planner, and Mike Bagheri,
  Transportation Development Manager, presented a PowerPoint
  presentation on the item; with all responding to questions. Laura
  Cornejo, Director of Transportation, responded to questions
  related to the Transportation's presentation on the updated
  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) and non-CEQA
  thresholds and caps; and the evaluation of accumulate impacts.
  Kathe Head, Managing Principal with Keyser Marston Associates,
  Inc. (City consultant), responded to questions related to the
  proposed project, base-zoning, and information contained in the
  comparative financial analysis.

  Councilmember Madison expressed concerns with developers
  utilizing density bonuses to avoid providing on-site affordable
  housing as part of their proposed projects; and spoke on the need
  to contact state legislators to provide equalizing legislation that
  provides some concessions and considerations to cities that have
  aggressive inclusionary housing ordinances.

  Councilmember Wilson requested that staff provide information
  on the updated Regional Housing Needs Assessment (RHNA)
  data including the methodology, and benchmarks. He also
  expressed concerns with information contained in the CEQA and
  non-CEQA analysis, particularly regarding the methodology of the
  analysis, which lacks cumulative impacts and the range of
  mitigation measures.

  Councilmember Gordo expressed concerns regarding the lack of
  measurements for cumulative impacts. He encouraged staff to
  investigate ways to better measure such impacts, and requested
  that staff consider utilizing this information to enact mitigation
  measures that would require developers to work with the City to
  help mitigate cumulative impacts. He also expressed concerns
  with the amount of additional square footage of the proposed
  revised project, specifically the increase from 60 to 75 feet in
  height. He requested that staff provide the draft RHNA formula to
  help determine the number of new units the City must build, with
  the formula serving as a basis for appeal or challenge, the timeline
  to appeal or challenge; and that a discussion on the RHNA
  formula and appeal process be agendized as soon as possible at
  a future City Council meeting.

Council Minutes  9  02/10/2020
   The following individuals spoke in opposition to the staff
  recommendation and/or provided comments related to the
  proposed project:

  Ken McCormick, Pasadena resident
  Andrew Salimian, representing Pasadena Heritage
  Nina Chomsky, Pasadena resident
  John Latia, representing Madison Heights Neighborhood
  Association (MHNA)
  Erika Foy, representing Livable Pasadena
  Suzie Boyer, representing MHNA
  Ryan Panzarella, Pasadena resident
  Megan Foker, Livable Pasadena

  Richard A. McDonald, representing the applicant, spoke in favor
  of the staff recommendation; clarified information related to the
  project; and responded to questions. Rob Tyler, Architect with
  Tyler+ Kelly Architecture, responded to questions related to the
  sites massing diagram.

  Vice Mayor Hampton expressed opposition to the inclusion of
  rental units as part of the proposed project. He suggested that it
  would be more beneficial to allow for units to be sold as affordable
  condominium units to promote affordable homeownership. He
  also expressed concerns that the proposed project is not in
  compliance with the City's General Plan and reiterated his request
  to consider updates to the General Plan as soon as possible. He
  concluded by stating he was unable to support the project.

  Councilmember McAustin spoke on the impacts that the various
  state legislative actions have had on the City, which are designed
  to increase the housing stock, addressing state housing shortages
  and affordability issues. She stated that she believes the project
  should be approved due to state legislation and to ensure that the
  City is meeting the requirements of state mandates. Additionally,
  she stated, insofar as the state is adopting laws that strip the City
  of its fundamental rights to self-govern and maintain local control,
  the City should push back against the state legislation.

  Councilmember Gordo expressed concerns that the proposed
  project provides few affordable housing units, and noted that the
  high density development is going to change the character of the
  surrounding area, which is also inconsistent with the General
  Plan. He expressed his desire for the City Council to consider
  rejoining the Council of Governments, as they are engaged with a
  joint powers of authority to bring more dollars for affordable
  housing to Pasadena; and in favor of working with other

Council Minutes  10  02/10/2020
   municipalities to push back on state legislation. He asked staff to
  provide additional information on the in-fill exemption so that the
  City Council may have a better understanding of cumulative
  impacts, the appropriateness of applying the exemption, and
  agendize at a future City Council meeting for discussion. Lastly,
  he expressed concerns with the procedure that was followed on
  this proposed project and believes that staff is not operating within
  the City's established rules.

  Councilmember Madison stated that he does not believe the
  process is procedurally flawed,, but reiterated his concerns that
  Pasadena (with robust inclusionary zoning legislation in place)
  and other cities with few, if any, inclusionary zoning requirements
  are subject to the same density bonus legislation.

  Mayor T ornek stated that he believes staff has responded to
  concerns and did a good job on this complicated project. He
  spoke on the need for the City Council to be mindful of the law,
  his preference that the City Council align with communities (i.e.
  Glendale, Burbank) who have made affordable housing efforts
  part of their General Plans; and spoke in favor of the staff
  recommendation.

  Councilmember Wilson expressed concerns with the flaws on how
  traffic impacts are measured, and the proposed project's
  inconsistency with the City's General Plan. He stated that the City
  Council has to follow the law and the proposed project comports
  with the law; and for staff to amplify the City's efforts to address
  the critical policy issues related to state legislation, and
  transportation.  He asked that staff work with the Design
  Commission to provide additional attentiveness to the projects site
  plan, specifically related to the tree preservation.

  Councilmember Kennedy spoke in opposition to any proposed
  litigation against the state related to affordable housing, including
  legislation that provides developers with housing concessions;
  and stated the need for the City to abide by state legislation and
  rules. He also spoke on the need to agendize at a future City
  Council meeting issues related to the usurpation of local control
  and governance by the State of California; and stated his support
  for the staff recommendation.
